This pathway is supported by the lowest common ancestor relationship between Cabazitaxel and Eribulin, both of which are classified as Tubulin Binding Agents, and their shared classification as Organic Molecular Entities. The integration of these relationships implies that Cabazitaxel exerts its effects via a mechanism that involves interaction with Tubb6, likely through a shared molecular pathway. The presence of a direct binding interaction between Eribulin and Tubb6, along with the established role of microtubule inhibitors in targeting tubulin, strengthens the hypothesis that Cabazitaxel may similarly interact with Tubb6. The evidence supports a mechanistic link between Cabazitaxel and Tubb6, though further experimental validation is required to confirm the exact nature of the interaction.
